draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kollur! This little temple town is home to the Mookambika Temple, which sits at the foot of the Kodachadri hills on the southern bank of the Souparnika River.
draft.hungryLine: Kollur is a small temple town, so keep it simple and eat at a local place near the temple.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Kollur Mookambika Temple is just a minute's walk away, and it's the reason everyone comes here.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot near the Souparnika River, right by the temple, and take in the Kodachadri foothills.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Mookambika Temple counts among both the 108 Durgalayas and the 108 Shivalayas, which is why it's considered so special.

spots.name: Kollur Mookambika Temple
spots.detail: 1 min walk · Temple of the mother goddess Mookambika

legends.title: Three goddesses in one
legends.body: Devotees see Mookambika as the union of Adi Parashakti and Parabramha. The Linga here is said to hold Maha Kali, Maha Lakshmi and Maha Saraswathi on its left side.

tips.title: Dress modestly for the temple.
tips.body: Kollur is a pilgrimage town and the Mookambika Temple is the heart of it.

tips.title: Walk down to the Souparnika.
tips.body: The temple stands on the river's southern bank, so it's an easy stroll from the shrine.

story.title: A coast made by Parashurama
story.body: Kollur lies in the land between Gokarna and Kanyakumari, which is believed to have been created by the sage Parashurama.

story.title: Home of Mookambika
story.body: The town grew around the Mookambika Temple, dedicated to the mother goddess and counted among the 108 Durgalayas and 108 Shivalayas.

story.title: A small town
story.body: The 2001 census counted 3,863 people in Kolluru, with 1,900 men and 1,962 women.

story.title: Temple town of Byndoor
story.body: Kollur is a temple town and village in Byndoor taluk of Udupi district, near Kundapur.
